subject: Data sovereignty clauses & subprocessor onboarding for Atlas Cloud
messages:
From: Elena Miranda <elena.miranda@atlas-cloud.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@atlas-cloud.com
Date: 2027-04-10T09:12:00Z
Subject: Subprocessor disclosure + UK addendum question

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for the demo last week — Atlas is excited about Redwood's latency profile. Procurement asked me to share the vendor/subprocessor list and a specific request from our legal team. Attached: atlas_subprocessor_list_v1.csv.

Two items they flagged:
1) We need confirmation that Redwood will sign our UK Addendum (we attached a sample redline). If you require exceptions, please call them out.
2) One of our processors (Third‑Party Analytics, a US company) will process event-level telemetry. Our team needs to understand whether you can accept a limited derogation or whether you insist on storing EU-origin data only within EU controls.

Finally, our security lead asked for a short, explicit "cessation of processing" clause that covers export/termination scenarios (they want to avoid continued forwarding of EU data after termination). I've included a suggested clause in the attachment (proposed_cessation_clause.txt).

Can you loop in legal and privacy and let us know the realistic path (UK Addendum + SCCs + subprocessor mapping + anything else)? Procurement would like to keep the timetable tight — target signature by end of month.

Best,

Elena Miranda
Head of Cloud Partnerships
Atlas Cloud

Attachments: atlas_subprocessor_list_v1.csv, proposed_cessation_clause.txt

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com
To: Elena Miranda <elena.miranda@atlas-cloud.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwoodinference.com, priyom_das@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-04-11T11:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Subprocessor disclosure + UK addendum question

Hi Elena — thanks for the materials and the clear asks. Looping in Monica (Customer Success) and Priyom (Privacy & Legal) to review the attachments and proposed clause. Quick notes from my side:

- We're generally able to execute the UK Addendum + SCCs pattern, but there may be a small redline on the cessation language (depends on the exact wording).
- Subprocessor onboarding is negotiable. For US-based analytics, we typically require documented safeguards (encryption at rest/in transit, access controls, and a DPA flowdown).
- Timeline: if legal can provide a cleaned redline by next week I can commit to getting procurement to sign the DPA + Addendum shortly after.

Monica/Priyom — can you take point on (a) reviewing the proposed_cessation_clause.txt, (b) confirming whether the Third‑Party Analytics profile triggers a DPIA or additional contractual controls, and (c) whether we need any changes to our subprocessor onboarding checklist?

Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: SCCs_redline_for_retail.docx (copied from Atlas for reference)

From: priyom_das@redwoodinference.com
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com, monica_patel@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Elena Miranda <elena.miranda@atlas-cloud.com>
Date: 2027-04-12T08:23:00Z
Subject: Re: Subprocessor disclosure + UK addendum question — legal read

Hi all,

Thanks for the context, Vivek and Elena. I reviewed atlas_subprocessor_list_v1.csv and the proposed cessation wording. Summary and suggested next steps below.

1) UK Addendum + SCCs approach
- We can accept the UK Addendum tied to the EU SCCs (standard two-step) but will propose a limited operational carve-out rather than a broad derogation. The carve-out would allow temporary cross-border routing for caching/edge delivery but not long-term storage or analytics outside EU/UK without prior consent.
- Redline in SCCs_redline_for_retail.docx: suggest replacing the phrase "may transfer" with "may temporarily route for delivery and telemetry purposes only; no onward storage or analytics beyond 30 days without prior written consent."

2) Third‑party analytics (US)
- This triggers our "elevated processor" flow. Required controls: AES‑256 at rest, TLS1.3 in transit, role‑based access, contractual DPA flowdown, SOC 2 Type II (or equivalent), and documented data minimization for telemetry.
- If Atlas insists on analytics outside EU/UK, we will require either (A) a specific TIA/DTIA between Atlas and the analytics vendor with Redwood listed as a subprocessor and data use restrictions, or (B) that the analytics vendor sign Redwood's DPA addendum with explicit purpose limitations.

3) Cessation of processing clause
- The proposed_cessation_clause.txt is close but needs two clarifications: (1) a concrete retention window post-termination (we usually propose 90 days for transitional needs, with an option to extend by mutual written agreement), and (2) an auditable confirmation mechanism (signed certificate from subprocessor within 30 days of deletion).
- I attach a draft clause snippet you can propose to Atlas: "Upon termination, Redwood and its subprocessors will cease processing Customer Data, delete or return Customer Data within 90 days, and provide a signed certification of deletion within 30 days of completion. Any exception requires written authorization signed by both parties specifying retention period and scope."

4) Timeline & next steps
- I can produce a concise redline of the SCCs + UK Addendum with the suggested carve-outs by EOD April 14.
- If Atlas can accept the 90‑day deletion window and the audit certificate, I don't foresee blockers for procurement to proceed.

I'll prepare the redline and the clause snippet and share the DocuSign-ready DPA once we have agreement on the retention window.

Best,
Priyom Das
Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwoodinference.com

Attachments referenced: proposed_cessation_clause.txt (review comments), internal_redline_notes.pdf

From: Elena Miranda <elena.miranda@atlas-cloud.com>
To: priyom_das@redwoodinference.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@atlas-cloud.com, sam.irving@analytics-srv.com
Date: 2027-04-13T13:47:00Z
Subject: Re: Subprocessor disclosure + UK addendum question — legal read

Hi Priyom — thanks for the clear read. A couple quick replies from Atlas legal/procurement:

- The 90‑day deletion window is acceptable to us provided we can retain limited aggregated telemetry for 12 months for trend analysis (non‑PII, fully aggregated). We propose adding a sentence to the cessation clause allowing aggregated, irreversible analytics retention.
- For the Third‑Party Analytics vendor: Sam (copied) can share SOC 2 docs and a separate DPA; procurement would prefer Option A (a TIA/DTIA between Atlas and the analytics vendor with Redwood listed).
- Procurement would like a clean redline in DocuSign by next Tuesday so they can include it in their contract bundle.

If you can reflect the aggregated telemetry carve-out and confirm the 30‑day deletion audit certificate, we'll be ready to route to procurement.

Best,
Elena

Attachments: none in this reply

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com
To: Elena Miranda <elena.miranda@atlas-cloud.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwoodinference.com, monica_patel@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-04-20T15:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Subprocessor disclosure + UK addendum question — final approach & DocuSign

Elena — quick status update and next steps.

1) Priyom finished the redline. Key changes included: 90‑day deletion window, 30‑day signed deletion certificate, temporary routing carve-out (30 days max unless mutually agreed), and an explicit allowance for aggregated, non‑reversible telemetry retained up to 12 months. The redline is uploaded to the Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cAtlasDPA (see SCCs_redline_for_retail.docx).

2) On subprocessors: we accept Option A — Atlas can run a TIA/DTIA with Third‑Party Analytics; Redwood must be listed as a subprocessor and must receive a copy of the DPA/TIA. We will require Sam's SOC 2 report and evidence of encryption controls before onboarding.

3) Procurement path: I've instructed our commercial ops to prepare the DocuSign envelope (link below). If Atlas confirms acceptance of the redline as-is, I'll send the envelope and route it for signature by Redwood legal/commercial.

DocuSign (prelim): https://app.docusign.com/prepare?envelopeId=DD-AC-2027-045

Proposed immediate actions:
- Elena/procurement: confirm the aggregated telemetry carve-out language is acceptable.
- Sam/Third‑Party Analytics: share SOC2 and encryption evidence (cc’d Sam for follow-up).
- Monica: I'll hand off to you for procurement coordination once Elena confirms.

If all good, we'll aim to complete signatures by April 26 and begin subprocessor onboarding the week after.

Thanks — Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: DocuSign envelope prepared; SCCs_redline_for_retail.docx (final redline)
